molecular Hamiltonian Lie algebra struct.description:
Simulation of molecular vibrations is emerging as a promising application of quantum computing in quantum chemistry. In this work, we develop new strategies for block-encoding the second-quantized n-mode representation of the vibrational Hamiltonian, whose algebraic structure closely parallels that of the second-quantized electronic Hamiltonian. We derive linear-combination-of-unitaries (LCU) representations of this Hamiltonian based on Pauli decomposition and tensor hypercontraction (THC) and construct efficient circuits for the corresponding block encodings. We also extend the Block-Invariant Symmetry Shift (BLISS) technique to vibrational Hamiltonians, yielding a lower LCU 1-norm and, consequently, a lower overall circuit cost. For the molecules considered here, BLISS-THC reduces the Toffoli cost of quantum phase estimation by more than two orders of magnitude relative to existing block-encoding approaches. In comparison with recent Trotter-based methods, it shows up to a ninefold reduction in the T-gate count, with the relative savings tending to increase with system size. Asymptotically, and up to polylogarithmic factors, both the Pauli and THC LCUs trade additional ancillas for a quadratic improvement in scaling with the number of modes, while THC provides an additional quadratic improvement in scaling with the number of modals. These results highlight the importance of Hamiltonian factorizations and Toffoli–qubit tradeoffs for reducing the computational cost of quantum simulations of molecular vibrations.

In this work, we focus on an alternative representation, the second-quantized n-mode representation of the vibrational Hamiltonian [44]. molecular Hamiltonian Lie algebra struct.title: Trotter simulation of vibrational Hamiltonians on a quantum computer
molecular Hamiltonian Lie algebra struct.description: > Abstract:Simulating vibrational dynamics is essential for understanding molecular structure, unlocking useful applications such as vibrational spectroscopy for high-fidelity chemical detection. Quantum algorithms for vibrational dynamics are emerging as a promising alternative to resource-demanding classical approaches, but this domain is largely underdeveloped compared to quantum simulations of electronic structure. In this work, we describe in detail three distinct forms of the vibrational Hamiltonian: canonical bosonic quantization, real space representation, and the Christiansen second-quantized form. Leveraging Lie algebraic properties of each, we develop efficient fragmentation schemes to enable the use of Trotter product formulas for simulating time evolution. We introduce circuits required to implement time evolution in each form, and highlight factors that contribute to the simulation cost, including the choice of vibrational coordinates. Using a perturbative approach for the Trotter error, we obtain tight estimates of T gate cost for the simulation of time evolution in each form, enabling their quantitative comparison. Combining tight Trotter error estimates and efficient fragmentation schemes, we find that for the medium-sized CH$_4$ molecule with 9 vibrational modes, time evolution for approximately 1.8 ps may be simulated using as little as 36 qubits and approximately $3 \times 10^{8}$ T gates -- an order-of-magnitude speedup over prior-art algorithms. Finally, we present calculations of vibrational spectra using each form to demonstrate the fidelity of our algorithms. This work presents a unified and highly optimized framework that makes simulating vibrational dynamics an attractive use case for quantum computers.

chemistry algebra Casimir operator exact.description: # Application of U(2)⊃O(2) and U(2)⊃U(1) dynamical symmetries to diatomic molecular vibrations ... ## Abstract Algebraic Hamiltonians based on the Casimir invariants of U(1) and O(2) dynamical symmetries of U(2) are used to describe the vibrational energy level spectrum of a diatomic molecule. The set of vibrational eigenstates arising from the U(1) chain remains closed under the operation of the appropriate ladder operators, whereas no such closure occurs in the case of the O(2) chain. This result is shown to be a consequence of the differing roles of the dimension of the irreducible representation of U(2), the so-called vibron number, in the two dynamical symmetry chains. A simple procedure is proposed to effect closure in the O(2) chain, as required for the eigenstates of a Morse oscillator Hamiltonian, to which the algebraic Hamiltonian based on the quadratic Casimir invariant of O(2) reduces within a coordinate representation. For each symmetry chain, application of the Holstein-Primakoff transformation leads to a set of ladder operators that act on one-dimensional harmonic oscillator eigenstates. Explicit comparison of the two dynamical symmetry chains is made with respect to the vibrational energy spectrum of the hydrogen molecule in its ground electronic state.

chemistry algebra Casimir operator exact.title: Solving the Kratzer oscillator in diatomic molecules: an algebraic approach based on the so(2,1) Lie algebra
chemistry algebra Casimir operator exact.description: Abstract In this article, we solve the rovibrational Schrödinger equation for diatomic molecules using the Kratzer oscillator by means of the so ( 2 , 1 ) Lie algebra. The main contribution of our algebraic approach is that this allows us to reduce the degree of the Schrödinger equation giving thus a first-order differential equation, by which the vibrational ground state wave function is obtained, clearly and in few steps. The energies are obtained by scaling of the observables r and p r which preserves the canonical commutation relation, and a recurrence relation for the bound states written in terms of the raising operator is also given. Also we calculate the rovibrational spectrum of H 2 and CO molecules, showing that the energies of the Kratzer oscillator not only depends on vibrational and rotational quantum numbers, but also in the difference between the vibrational quantum number with its minimum value, for a fixed l . The article ends giving a physical insight of the symmetry transformation of the SO (2, 1) Lie group in order to show the relationship between this group and its associated Lie algebra. Finally, as an illustrative example, we calculated the selection rules for the vibrational quantum number, from a purely algebraic approach.

We discuss the finite-N Hilbert space of bilocal operators that underlies bilocal holography of vector models, beyond the sector built on the Fock vacuum. If the microscopic oscillator Fock space carries a multiplicity-free dual action of a compact color group G and a bilocal algebra, Howe duality implies that projection to the derived subgroup [G,G] selects precisely the characters of the abelianization G^(ab)=G/[G,G] that occur in the Fock space. Thus O(N)/SO(N)=Z_2 gives two sectors, U(N)/SU(N)=U(1) gives integer determinant-charge sectors, while Sp(N) is perfect and gives no additional sector; Bose/Fermi statistics and the number of modes determine which sectors are actually realized. We construct the epsilon and determinant backgrounds that generate these sectors, together with their finite-N constraints and Casimirs, and find that the two bosonic O(N) sectors are not distinguished by any Casimir. Using group-integral projectors, we derive explicit sector-resolved characters for the O(N) and U(N) theories. Around each new background we solve the constraints with auxiliary oscillators, which form a Fermi sea for bosonic matter. In the free vector model on R×S^2 the lowest states in the new sectors are baryonic primaries; we determine their energies, degeneracies and spin content exactly at finite N, together with their lowest energy at fixed angular momentum.

We characterize the hybrid Fourier transform on the Schwartz–Grassmann space 𝒮(ℝ^m)⊗Λ_(2n) by operator intertwining relations. Using the bosonic oscillator Howe decomposition and the fermionic Lefschetz decomposition, we describe the action of the hybrid Fourier transform on both tensor factors. We show that first-order covariance with respect to coordinate multiplication and differentiation determines the transform up to a scalar. Landau models serve as quantum mechanical systems for generating quantum matrix geometries. In this paper, we demonstrate that Howe duality provides the underlying structure of the super Landau model, reflecting a general feature of coset-type Landau models. The (super) Howe duality relates different Landau levels and accounts for the emergence of a dual fuzzy geometry. By employing super-spinor derivative operators, the supermonopole harmonics in both integer and half-integer Landau levels are explicitly constructed and the algebraic structure of the super-Hilbert space is revealed. We propose a consistent probabilistic interpretation for these wavefunctions defined on a supermanifold. Through a level projection method, we derive the matrix coordinates of fuzzy supersphere geometries for arbitrary Landau levels, along with a precise determination of the non-commutative scale factor. It is shown that the theta correspondence of Howe duality induces a geometric transformation between fuzzy objects. Finally, we point out that Howe duality realizes an internal-external space duality and underlies quantum matrix geometries, suggesting that it may play a fundamental role in understanding Matrix model geometries.

Using the newly defined inner product, the supermatrix coordinates are evaluated for arbitrary Landau levels. Viewing Howe duality as a duality between internal and external spaces, we argue that it is a general feature of coset-type Landau models and may underlie the geometric structure of quantum geometries in Matrix models.
